name: SeedVR2
plain: SeedVR2 (Wang et al., ByteDance Seed, 2025): upscales and restores photos and video frames x2 with a large diffusion transformer run for a single step; 3 B and 7 B versions, the 7 B runs on 16 GB with weight streaming (default, ~17 GB free host RAM). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: SeedVR2 (Wang et al., ByteDance Seed 2025): one-step video restoration and super-resolution by a diffusion transformer (NaDiT, adversarially post-trained) on the latents of a causal 3-D VAE. `seedvr2-3b` and `seedvr2-7b` are the 3 B and 7 B transformers (same VAE); frames are restored one at a time.

papers.title: SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training

licence_notes: The converted weight files (bf16 transformer with the fixed prompt embedding, bf16 VAE) are hosted by fastforks under the originals' Apache-2.0 licence; NOTICE keeps the attribution and lists the changes.
limitations: Generative restoration: the output depends on `seed` (one CPU generator draws the VAE posterior noise and the diffusion noise, upstream's default 666); other seeds give other plausible details.
One frame per call: the clip mode of the original (temporal attention over 4n + 1 frames) is not used by this image API.

The input is padded on the bottom and right (replicate) so that `scale x` its size is a multiple of 16, and the output cropped back; the original centre-crops the resized frame to a multiple of 16 instead.
No colour fix: the authors' scripts optionally match the output colours to the input with StableSR's wavelet reconstruction (non-commercial code), which is not included.

The 3 B model needs ~7 GB for its weights plus the VAE's activations (~14 GB peak at 960 x 1696 output); `stream=False` keeps them resident; by default (`stream=True`, CUDA) they stay in ~6.6 GB of page-locked host RAM (~9 GB peak at that size).

The 7 B model's weights are 16.5 GB in bf16: it runs with the default `stream=True` (blocks in ~16.5 GB of page-locked host RAM; load fails with an error when less is free) or `quant="nf4"` (~4.6 GB resident); with `stream=false` and no quant it runs out of GPU memory.

`quant="nf4"` changes the generated detail: 23-27 dB PSNR against the bf16 output (3 B, 4 clips; 7 B: 26-31 dB, 2 clips), about as far as another `seed` (18-24 dB), with ~3.5x smaller transformer blocks.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

variants.name: seedvr2-3b

licence.training_note: Paper (arXiv 2506.05301): adversarial post-training of SeedVR on large-scale image and video data with synthetic degradations; the data sources and terms are not stated.

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 8, padded to a multiple of 8

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 3 after 1 first call (the authors' generation loop with the DiT moved to the CPU during VAE encode / decode, their default), uint8 input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad + bf16 autocast; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: load: the authors' fp32 .pth files from the page cache (read once before)

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.02 vs the original. GPU, bfloat16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.01 and p99 <= 0.05 (absolute error of the output `image`).
